title: Ex Vivo Recording of Axonal Transport Dynamics on Postnatal Organotypic Cortical Slices
protocol: Weigh the mouse to define the amount of analgesic to administer pre- and post-surgery.
Prepare buprenorphine (Buprecare®) at a dilution of 0.03 mg/mL to administer 0.1 mg/kg.
Sedate the pregnant dam in an induction chamber with a mixture of 96% air and 4% isoflurane.
Monitor the breathing rate to assess the state of sedation, which takes approximately 60 seconds.
Transfer the mouse quickly onto a heating pad with the abdomen facing down to prevent hypothermia.
Apply ophthalmic lubricant (Fucithalmic Vet®) to both eyes to prevent corneal drying.
Inject buprenorphine subcutaneously within the loose skin over the interscapular area.
Place the mouse's nose inside a mask respirator with the abdomen facing up.
Adjust the concentration of isoflurane vaporized to 2%.
Monitor anesthesia depth closely to prevent insufficient sedation or respiratory/cardiac depression.
Check toe pinch response to assess anesthesia depth.
Observe respiration rate; optimal range is approximately 1 breath/s under proper anesthesia.
Adjust anesthetic flow rate if necessary to reach optimal anesthesia depth.
Perform in utero cortical electroporation within 20–25 minutes, not exceeding 30 minutes for optimal viability.
Shave the abdomen of the pregnant dam with a depilatory cream.
Disinfect the shaved area with a 70% alcoholic solution.
Make an incision of approximately 1.5 cm along the skin abdomen midline first, then cut through the peritoneum.
Place a surgical field with a rhomboidal aperture over the abdomen.
Wet the drape and the open abdominal cavity with warm saline.
Carefully pull the uterus out from the abdominal cavity using ring forceps at the gaps between embryos.
Expose one of the two uterine horns on the surgical drape.
Apply warm sterile phosphate-buffered saline (PBS) solution to prevent drying of the embryos during the procedure.
Cut diagonally the tip of a previously pulled microcapillary.
Hold an embryo with ring forceps or fingers.
Insert the microcapillary through the uterus into one of the lateral ventricles of the embryo.
Inject approximately 0.5 μL of DNA plasmid mix using a mouth-controlled tube or a foot pedal-activated microinjector.
Monitor the success of injection by observing the green dye filling the ventricles.
Place the anode on the injection site and the cathode on the opposite side of the brain.
Hold the injected embryo with ring forceps to stabilize its position while placing the electrodes over the target site for electroporation.
Deliver electrical impulses by pressing the foot pedal of the electroporator.
Observe the formation of bubbles around the electrodes as an indication of correct impulse delivery.
Hydrate the uterine horn after plasmid injection and electroporation.
Slide the hydrated uterine horn gently back into the abdomen cavity.
Repeat the procedure on the second uterine horn.
Suture the skin and muscle layers separately to prevent bleeding.
Transfer the mouse to a cage under a warming light with paper towels for monitoring.
Monitor the mouse closely until recovery from anesthesia.
Document the well-being of the mouse daily by checking surgical wounds, appearance, and behavior.
Dissect brains of electroporated pups at postnatal day two (P2).
Embed dissected brains into an agarose matrix for mechanical support.
Decapitate the P2 pup with surgical scissors.
Carefully dissect out the full brain including olfactory bulbs, forebrain, and hindbrain.
Collect the dissected brain into a petri dish containing ice-cold HBSS.
Place embedding molds on ice.
Pour the 4% agarose solution that was previously brought to 37°C into the molds.
Remove excess HBSS from the brain.
Transfer the brain into the agarose solution.
Rotate the brain gently and repeatedly within the agarose solution using forceps.
Continue rotating until the brain is steady in the final position with olfactory bulbs facing upwards and coronal axis parallel to the mold bottom.
Let the agarose block solidify on ice for about 15 minutes.
Set the vibratome by filling the vibratome tray with cold HBSS and the vibratome bath with ice.
Adjust the sectioning parameters for a Leica VT100S vibratome: set section thickness to 300 μm, cutting speed to 3, and cutting frequency to 3.
Coat the glass-bottom dish with a thin layer of culture medium containing Matrigel by adding 1 mL solution and aspirating back most of the volume.
Keep the coated dish at room temperature (below the polymerizing temperature of 37°C).
Shape the agarose block around the brain by making a cut at the rostral and ventral sides, parallel to each other and to the sectioning plane, approximately 0.5 cm from the brain surface.
Remove excess agarose also at the ventral and dorsal sides of the brain.
Cut the block with a truncated pyramid shape ensuring the olfactory bulbs face the minor base for increased adhesion surface and stability.
Embed the brain in a 4% agarose solution ensuring optimal positioning until polymerization.
Shape the agarose block to ensure a thickness of 0.5 cm from the brain surface.
Glue the agarose block onto the vibratome tray platform with the olfactory bulbs facing upwards.
Fix the platform with the glued agarose block into the vibratome tray filled with cold HBSS.
Section the agarose block to generate coronal slices containing the callosal projections crossing the midline.
Collect the brain sections in a dish filled with ice-cold HBSS.
Check the collected slices for fluorescence.
Transfer onto coated MatTek dishes only the slices with the electroporated region of interest.
Carefully manipulate the brain slices to avoid separation from surrounding agarose.
Keep embedded brains at 4°C during sectioning by regularly changing HBSS and refilling vibratome bath with ice.
Cover each slice with a drop of culture medium containing Matrigel using a pipette.
Place glass-bottom dishes in incubator at 37°C and 5% CO2 for 20 minutes to allow Matrigel to polymerize and slices to recover.
Use ice-cold reagents and perform all manipulations on ice to minimize step times due to short survival time of postnatal cultured organotypic brain slices (approximately 4 h).
Record transport dynamics of fluorescently labeled organelles/vesicles along projections of callosal neurons for 2 hours after recovery in incubator.
Use a 63× oil lens with a working distance of 0.14 mm.
Position the bottom-glass dish within a recording chamber controlled at 37°C and 5% CO2.
Acquire time-lapse images using a confocal microscope for a desired capturing time at the corpus callosum midline to discriminate directionality of transport.
Image at least three frames per second for 60 seconds.
Set microscope lasers at a power low enough to visualize cargos for the entire acquisition time.

Locate the corpus callosum midline by first using the 10× lens to identify fluorescently labeled neurons in the electroporated hemisphere of the brain slice and follow neuronal projections to the midline.
Restrain the animal with the ventral abdomen facing up and the head slightly tilted downward for IP injection.
Insert the syringe at 4–5 mm depth into the lower right quadrant of the abdomen toward the mouse head, maintaining a 20°–30° angle to the abdominal surface.
Aspirate by pulling back the syringe plunger to check if vital organs were punctured and if any fluid is aspirated.
If no fluid is aspirated, inject slowly the tamoxifen solution; if fluid is observed, withdraw and discard the needle.
Gently perform the procedure again with a new needle for each animal.
Observe the animal to check for signs of bleeding at injection site or signs of pain or distress due to complications of injection.
